cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-woven strip-cloth boubou/tobe gown with indigo dye and white embroidered knot motifs, a garment type characteristic of West African peoples including the Wolof of Senegal. It clearly shows a made garment plausible for the claimed culture and region.

physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Gown (tobe, boubou, riga), with wide flared sleeves, composed of 69 cotton strips hand- woven and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. Each narrow strip is composed of hand-spun dark and light indigo and magenta ‘alaari’ warps, and dark indigo wefts. This The garment has two pockets left open in the front, which are lined with narrow strips of the same fabric. The areas around the neck and the pockets are embroidered in white cotton bordering the openings, and there are also eleven knots. The neck embroidery continues down the back of the garment ending in a large knot. The open edges of the garment are hemmed by hand.
